item.title: Trump imposed additional tariffs on India to apply ‘secondary pressure’ on Moscow
item.description: Donald Trump increased tariffs on Indian goods. The White House stated this was to pressure Russia to end the Ukraine conflict. This followed meetings between Trump and Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Trump aims for trilateral talks with Vladimir Putin. India is concerned about replacing Russian oil imports. European leaders are reportedly grateful for Trump's insights into Russia's position.

item.title: Maryvale High School stabbing: One student killed, another injured in Phoenix
item.description: A violent altercation at Maryvale High School in Phoenix resulted in the death of one student and injuries to another. The incident, involving a stabbing, prompted a lockdown and an immediate response from a campus safety officer. Authorities are investigating the tragedy, which has deeply affected the school community and prompted calls for increased safety measures.

item.title: Katherine Clark retracts 'genocide' label: Not accusing Israel; calls for aid, hostages return
item.description: Katherine Clark, a top Democrat in the US House, addressed her recent remarks. She clarified that she was not accusing Israel of genocide. This came after she used the term 'genocide' at an event. Her statement aimed to clarify her position. She emphasized the need for humanitarian aid to Palestinians. She also called for the release of hostages.

item.title: Epstein files fallout: Trump appoints Missouri AG Andrew Bailey as FBI co‑deputy; to share role with Dan Bongino
item.description: President Trump appointed Andrew Bailey as co-deputy FBI director to address internal tensions over the Epstein case. Bailey, a Trump loyalist, will serve alongside Dan Bongino, potentially leading to Bongino's exit. This unconventional appointment, lacking FBI experience, signals a shift towards Trump's priorities within the bureau amid scrutiny of Epstein file management.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Texas Dem Nicole Collier refuses police monitoring: Spends night on House floor; protests redistricting
item.description: Texas Representative Nicole Collier staged an overnight protest on the House floor, defying Republican demands for police monitoring amid a redistricting standoff. Collier's act followed a Democratic walkout aimed at blocking the GOP's redrawn Congressional map. Her protest drew support and arrests, highlighting the intense political battle over redistricting in Texas.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Gavin’s tit-for-tat move: Proposes special election to counter Texas redistricting; sparks GOP outrage
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom is pushing for a special election to redraw congressional maps, responding to Republican redistricting in Texas. Critics, including Republicans and former Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger, decry the move as undermining independent redistricting. The proposal aims to bolster Democratic seats, sparking legal challenges and debate over democratic principles versus political advantage.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Concert chaos at Rose Bowl: Woman knocked unconscious in wild attack - Watch
item.description: A Rüfüs Du Sol concert at the Rose Bowl turned violent when a man assaulted a woman after a drink was spilled on him. The attacker returned, issued death threats, and then punched the woman unconscious, causing severe facial injuries. Police are investigating the incident, and Rüfüs Du Sol has condemned the violence, urging witnesses to come forward.

item.title: Crime stats scandal in DC: Justice dept opens probe; possible manipulation alleged
item.description: The Justice Department is investigating the Washington, DC, Metropolitan Police Department (MPD) for allegedly manipulating crime data to falsely portray a decrease in crime rates. This inquiry, led by the US Attorney’s office for DC, follows allegations against commander Michael Pulliam, who is accused of altering crime data and has been placed on paid leave.

item.title: UAE: No more second-term exams for students across all grades in 2025–26 academic year
item.description: The UAE Ministry of Education has cancelled second-semester central exams for all grades, shifting to continuous and school-based assessments to ease academic pressure and improve learning outcomes. Grades 1–4 will follow continuous evaluation, while grades 5–12 will have summative school assessments. The 2025–26 academic year begins August 25, with nine new schools, updated infrastructure, and over one million students returning.

item.title: UAE: Sharjah is bringing solar-powered trailers in the mountains without Wi-Fi or lights for true nature escape
item.description: Sharjah is expanding its eco-tourism portfolio with Nomad, an off-grid retreat of 20 solar-powered trailers launching in Kalba in late 2025. As part of the Sharjah Collection by Shurooq, Nomad emphasizes digital detox and nature immersion. The collection now spans seven retreats, reflecting the emirate’s commitment to sustainable, culturally rooted, and environmentally conscious hospitality experiences.
